_note: JSE conformance corpus — OPTIONAL CALL + DESTRUCTURING ASSIGNMENT (2026-08-12, the syntax-004 follow-up). Two constructs previously ratified as 'absent with a workaround' are now grammar, because the workaround kept being written: `o.f?.()` (a nullish callee answers null with the ARGS UNEVALUATED — the JS rule; a non-lambda callee also answers null where JS throws, because JSE is total) and `[a, b] = [b, a]` (the declaration-less array-pattern write — parseDeclarators reads the same shape a `const` reads, bound with the ASSIGNMENT writer, RHS evaluated ONCE before any binding). Object-pattern assignment `({a} = o)` remains undeclared grammar — a declaration covers it — and labelled break remains ratified-absent. Scope: Swift = reference, Kotlin :core via ConformanceTest, TS both tiers via conformance.test.ts.
